pairs.difference: A: the white panels stay a cool lilac-grey, and the red is a true red against the orange sand. B: the white panels turn peach-cream towards the bottom, the top panel red leans orange, and a large red-orange shadow fills the sand, so the whole ball sits in one warm cast. A is the louder card, which is why confidence is low.
pairs.fix: Keep the white panels a clean cool white with soft grey-lilac shading, not peach. Make the red panel a true red, not orange-red. Make the shadow on the sand a darker sand brown, not red.

pairs.difference: A: the green wall is muted and dark, giving the red booth and white target a calm surround. B: the brick wall is a loud pure lime green, the frame and shelf are saturated orange, and the target blue is pure. Hero and background are equally loud, and both chroma readings sit above the real range. The extra gold cans and striped props add more loud spots.
pairs.fix: Make the wall a muted, darker green. Make the wood a calm honey brown. Keep the strongest color on the target only.

pairs.difference: A: yellow-lime stripes, a saturated cyan airflow and an extra orange cushion, plant and red and blue books spread the palette across many hues. B: a muted green wall, with the unit's side falling to a cool periwinkle like the real computer's blue side. B's green cast is itself unusually strong (warm share 0, shadow chroma 2.28), so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Lower the wall to a soft muted green. Remove the orange cushion and the bright books. Shade the white unit with cool blue-grey and make the air a pale, thin blue.

pairs.difference: A: bright cyan water, cream-yellow sand, a hot pink shell and magenta and blue gems, with orange gold throughout, giving 6.47 hue families, above the real range. B: deeper blue water, sand falling to grey-violet on the right, a pale shell and gold that stays closer to neutral yellow, so there are resting areas.
pairs.fix: Use a deeper blue sea and a paler sand that turns grey-blue in shadow. Make the shell a pale dusty pink. Make the gems small and the gold less orange.

pairs.difference: A: orange wood with a real blue-navy band and visor, and a clean white crown. B: the whole card falls into a sepia cast. The white crown turns tan, the navy goes brown-black in the lens, the visor picks up brown, and subject and background chroma both fall below the real range. A's orange floor is loud, but its local colors hold.
pairs.fix: Keep the cap crown clean white and the band clearly navy blue. Make the wood floor a brighter, cleaner golden brown with no brown tint over the whole picture.

pairs.difference: A: a pure red booth on a saturated green wall with a lime glow behind it, plus teal glass, a gold crown and a yellow handle, so subject chroma sits above the real range. B: a greyer green background, with booth shadows falling to deep crimson, and fewer accents.
pairs.fix: Remove the lime glow behind the booth and make the green background quieter and greyer. Let the red fall to deep crimson on the shaded side. Use one small gold accent only.

pairs.difference: A: the cuffs are a true near-black with a cool blue reflection, giving a neutral rest beside the red. B: the gloves go coral with peach highlights, the cuff turns red-brown, and subject chroma is the higher of the two, so the red spreads through everything. The dusty blue wall in B is calm, and A's dark shadows read below the real range, so this is a weak call.
pairs.fix: Make the gloves a deep true red without coral or peach highlights. Make the wrist straps neutral black with a cool sheen.

pairs.difference: A: hot magenta-violet background with a bright pink glow behind the fins, and an orange rim on the yellow blades, so the background and hero compete at full chroma. B: a calmer violet, with near-neutral grey-black inserts and a darker grey-plum foot pocket. Both backgrounds exceed the real range, but A is further out.
pairs.fix: Make the background a calmer, darker violet with no pink glow. Make the foot pockets dark grey-plum and drop the orange rim on the yellow fins.

pairs.difference: A: a limited set of teal water, orange wood, red ring and rope tan, with dark blue-teal shadows on the posts under water. B: blue sky, cyan water, green palm, red hibiscus, orange starfish and golden rope, all at similar loudness, for 6.67 hue families, above the real range. The wood stays warm orange even in shade.
pairs.fix: Remove the palm, flower and starfish. Keep to teal water, brown wood and one red ring. Let the wood turn cool dark teal-brown where it meets the water.

pairs.difference: A: a softer orchid pink background, a natural brown-gold trunk and pale neutral stones. B: hot magenta background, an orange-red trunk that has lost its wood color, saturated yellow sand, and a magenta-red shadow. Background chroma is 0.2145, above the real range.
pairs.fix: Soften the background to a dusty pink. Make the trunk natural brown wood. Make the sand pale, the rocks grey-white and the shadow a darker sand tone.

pairs.difference: A: saturated violet wall against pure orange locker, with red, blue and green books and royal blue shoes, so hero and background are equally loud and both chroma readings exceed the real range. B: a dusty lilac wall, pale floor and white skirting give resting neutral areas behind an amber locker, and the contents are subdued.
pairs.fix: Make the wall a dusty greyed lilac. Make the floor pale wood. Mute the books to soft faded colors so the orange locker is the only loud color.

pairs.difference: A: pure green slide, cyan water, yellow tower, cobalt ladder, on pink and coral waves, with 7.15 hue families and subject chroma, both above the real range. B: one soft green slide and pillars with a cyan ladder and a small yellow deck, for 5.12 families, so the hero reads as one mass.
pairs.fix: Limit the slide and supports to one green. Keep one small yellow accent. Reduce the colored parts and leave the tiles pale and neutral.

pairs.difference: A: a blue-violet ring background with a yellow body that holds one hue, and white earbuds with cool violet shading. B: hot purple background with a pink glow, the yellow body shifts to orange-red at the bottom, and the white parts turn pink. Background chroma 0.2791 is far above the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the background a calmer blue-violet with no glow. Keep the player one yellow, shading to a deeper amber instead of red-orange. Keep the earbuds white with cool grey-violet shading.

pairs.difference: A: a deep green background darkens at the edges, the envelope is a muted cream, and the stamp and postmark are dusty rose. B: a neon green glow surrounds a peach-orange envelope with lilac shadow edges and a hot pink stamp. Background chroma is 0.25, above A and above the real range.
pairs.fix: Make the background a deep, calmer green without the bright center. Make the envelope a pale neutral cream with a dusty rose stamp and postmark.

pairs.difference: A: a muted tan wood table gives the vivid fruit a neutral rest. Its background chroma is just below the real range. B: orange stripes and an orange shelf sit behind fruit of the same warmth, with a pure blue berry mass and pale yellow-green grapes, so the background and hero compete. The gap is small.
pairs.fix: Replace the orange stripes with a plain muted tan wood surface. Make the grapes a deeper natural green and the blueberries a dusty dark blue.

pairs.difference: A: pure blue door, saturated orange frame, lime leaves, pink flowers and peach paving, with subject chroma 0.1742, above the real range, and warm share about double B's. B: the door is strong, but the ivy is a natural deeper green, the frame is a muted brown-orange and the wall is pale, so only the door is loud.
pairs.fix: Make the leaves a natural deep green. Make the door frame a muted brown. Keep the wall pale and let the blue door be the only saturated area.

pattern: The generated cards spend chroma everywhere. Hero and background are equally loud, and glows or halos behind the object push the background chroma above the real range. Neutrals are lost: whites turn cream or peach, greys pick up the card's warm cast, and materials such as leather and wood move to pure orange. Hues shift, with reds going orange-red and blues going cyan. Shadows stay warm or red instead of falling to cool, related darks. Extra props add more loud hue families, where real cards keep a quiet surround and let one mass carry the color. A rarer failure is the opposite: a sepia or single-hue cast over the whole card that erases local colors.
